post.description:
Aligns the target lap to the reference lap by distance (analysis at 1 m), then returns both laps' channels, the cumulative time delta and the Phase 3 verified findings. Every array has `meta.points` entries aligned to `distance_m`; booleans are JSON booleans; missing samples are null. Either lap may be `"fastest"`. Laps not valid for comparison are rejected (422) with the reason.

**Sign convention:** delta_s = target elapsed time − reference elapsed time at the same distance. Positive = the target is behind (has lost time); negative = the target is ahead. delta_s[0] is 0 and delta_s[-1] equals the official lap-time gap (target − reference) within 0.02 s.

Responses are gzip-compressed when the client sends `Accept-Encoding: gzip`, and memoized in-process (`meta.cached`).

post.description: Follow-up Q&A (≤ 300 characters after control characters are stripped). Out-of-scope questions are refused without an LLM call; the conversation keeps its last 6 turns server-side (in memory, never persisted). Every number is computed by the analysis engine; the AI only phrases the verified facts. `generated_by` says who wrote the text (llm | template | router), `outcome` how it got there (a template is served when the LLM is disabled, unavailable or its text failed validation, with `fallback_reason`), `facts` holds every cited fact and `segments` maps fact prefixes to finding ids. Non-streaming: nothing reaches the client before it passes the validator.

get.description: Uses only laps ≤ `lap` (all drivers, for the 6A exclusion rules) and the driver's current stint. Needs ≥ 5 clean laps in the stint, otherwise `status: insufficient_data` with a `reason` and no predictions or window. The pit window is a heuristic (interval_crossing_v2): it ignores undercut/overcut, traffic, track position, safety-car probability and tyre availability. Any field that cannot be computed is null and explained in `warnings`.
